title.en: Read between the lines at a family dinner
title.es: Leer entre líneas en una cena familiar

es: Integrar el bloque en una cena familiar: interpretar tres réplicas indirectas, responder a dos con tacto y cerrar con una question tag.

vocabulary.es: sacar conclusiones de, darle demasiadas vueltas a

teaching.en: Is that all you're having for dinner? From a mother who has spent all afternoon cooking, this is rarely a question about quantity.
teaching.es: ¿Eso es todo lo que vas a cenar? Viniendo de una madre que se ha pasado toda la tarde cocinando, rara vez es una pregunta sobre cantidad.
teaching.explanationEs: La pregunta es literal por fuera, pero el mensaje implícito es «come más» o «¿no te gusta?».
segments: Is that all you're having for dinner? From a mother who has
spent all afternoon cooking, this is rarely a question about quantity.
teaching.audioText: Is that all you're having for dinner? From a mother who has spent all afternoon cooking, this is rarely a question about quantity.

teaching.en: 'Nobody ever asks for seconds these days,' she sighed, which was her way of trying to drop a hint without sounding critical.
teaching.es: «Hoy en día nadie repite plato», suspiró, que era su manera de soltar una indirecta sin parecer crítica.
teaching.explanationEs: Drop a hint es sugerir algo sin pedirlo; seconds es repetir plato en la mesa.
segments: 'Nobody ever asks for seconds these days,' she sighed, which was
her way of trying to drop a hint without sounding critical.
teaching.audioText: 'Nobody ever asks for seconds these days,' she sighed, which was her way of trying to drop a hint without sounding critical.

teaching.en: I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? That is a diplomatic answer: it refuses the food without refusing the kindness.
teaching.es: No podría comer ni un bocado más, pero el postre se ve delicioso, ¿verdad? Es una respuesta diplomática: rechaza la comida sin rechazar el cariño.
teaching.explanationEs: Diplomatic es cuidar la relación mientras dices que no; la tag pide coincidir y cierra con calidez.
segments: I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? That
is a diplomatic answer: it refuses the food without refusing the kindness.
teaching.audioText: I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? That is a diplomatic answer: it refuses the food without refusing the kindness.

teaching.en: 'Some relatives only call when they need something,' he said with a pointed glance at his cousin, who pretended not to notice.
teaching.es: «Algunos parientes solo llaman cuando necesitan algo», dijo con una mirada intencionada a su primo, que fingió no darse cuenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Some + generalización y una pointed glance dirigen el reproche a alguien concreto sin nombrarlo.
segments: 'Some relatives only call when they need something,' he said with
a pointed glance at his cousin, who pretended not to notice.
teaching.audioText: 'Some relatives only call when they need something,' he said with a pointed glance at his cousin, who pretended not to notice.

teaching.en: The leftovers were so good that I'd happily take some home, but I try not to read into every comment at the table.
teaching.es: Las sobras estaban tan buenas que me llevaría algunas a casa con gusto, pero intento no darle demasiadas vueltas a cada comentario de la mesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Read into es deducir más de lo que se dice; a veces una frase es solo una frase.

I try not to read into every comment at the table.

teaching.en: When your aunt makes a pointed remark about your plate, it is often wiser to let it slide than to start an argument at dinner.
teaching.es: Cuando tu tía hace un comentario intencionado sobre tu plato, suele ser más sensato dejarlo pasar que empezar una discusión durante la cena.
teaching.explanationEs: Let it slide es no responder a una provocación pequeña; combina la interpretación con la decisión de no reaccionar.

prompt.es: Elige qué espera de verdad la abuela con su comentario sobre el arroz.

choices.text: She hopes that somebody will ask for more rice.
She is proud that nobody wastes her cooking.
She wants to know who cooked the rice this time.

feedback.es: Las fuentes llenas y el comentario sobre que nadie termina el arroz dejan ver la petición implícita: que alguien pida más.

hint.es: Mira las fuentes llenas: ¿qué echa de menos la abuela?

origin.text: Grandma looks at the full serving dishes on the table and says, 'Nobody ever finishes my rice these days.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Gracias, pero de verdad no puedo comer más.»

feedback.es: Con can't, el inglés usa any o anything y no nothing: la doble negación no refuerza sino que se evita.

hint.es: Tras una negación se usa la palabra que significa «alguno» o «nada».

origin.text: Thank you, but I really can't eat ___ more. I'm so full that I couldn't manage another bite.

answer.text: The cake looks lovely doesn't it

feedback.es: La coletilla repite el verbo de la frase (looks → doesn't it) y pide al oyente que coincida.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué intenta conseguir la madre al ofrecer más arroz.

choices.text: She supports the aunt's criticism with a friendly gesture.
She tries to lower the tension with a change of subject.
She wants to make sure that her cousin eats something at last.

feedback.es: El silencio tras el reproche de la tía hace que la madre ofrezca arroz: es un modo amable de cambiar de tema y relajar el ambiente.

origin.audio: At the family lunch, my aunt looked around the table and sighed, Some people only come when there is free food. Everyone went quiet, because we all knew that she was talking about my cousin, who had not visited for months. My mother quickly offered everyone more rice to change the subject, and my cousin, who had just arrived, smiled and said, I'm here for the company, but the rice does look lovely.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada réplica con su mensaje implícito.

pairs: Some relatives only call when they need something.

feedback.es: Cada réplica esconde una petición, una queja o un reproche; la última es la respuesta diplomática que los esquiva con cariño.

pairs: Some relatives only call when they need something.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta diplomática a la segunda ración de tu tía.

choices.text: It's delicious, and I'm full. Please stop serving me food.
I'm full, but I'd love another plate of everything.
It's delicious, but I'm full. Could I have some later?

feedback.es: Elogiar la comida, rechazar con amabilidad y proponer algo para más tarde protege la relación; las otras dos rechazan con dureza o aceptan sin ganas.

origin.text: Your aunt serves you a very large second helping after you have already eaten a lot. You are full, but you do not want to upset her.

prompt.es: Escucha a tu tío y elige a quién critica de forma indirecta.

choices.text: A relative who rarely visits the family.
His hosts, for inviting relatives only once a year.
Nobody at all; it is just a general remark about families.

feedback.es: Some people can only visit once a year y la sonrisa dirigida al primo apuntan a quien visita poco: es una crítica que se oculta tras un brindis.

origin.audio: It's lovely to see everyone here today, said my uncle, raising his glass. Some people can only visit once a year, of course, and that's perfectly fine. He smiled at my cousin, who studied his plate. After a silence, my grandmother quickly asked who wanted dessert.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige por qué pregunta la abuela quién quiere postre.

choices.text: To make sure nobody leaves before dessert.
To change the subject and calm the atmosphere.
To support the uncle's comment about visits.

feedback.es: Tras el silencio incómodo, preguntar por el postre es una forma de cambiar de tema y calmar el ambiente sin entrar en el reproche.

origin.audio: It's lovely to see everyone here today, said my uncle, raising his glass. Some people can only visit once a year, of course, and that's perfectly fine. He smiled at my cousin, who studied his plate. After a silence, my grandmother quickly asked who wanted dessert.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué piensa el abuelo del postre, por lo que dice y hace?

choices.text: He thinks it is nothing special but is being polite.
He dislikes it but is too proud to admit that he asked for more.
He likes it a lot but will not say so openly.

feedback.es: Not bad en boca de alguien que lo critica todo, más una segunda ración sin palabras, revelan que el postre le encanta aunque lo atenúe.

origin.text: At the end of the meal, your grandfather, who criticises everything, tastes the dessert, says 'Not bad' and serves himself a second helping without another word.

prompt.es: Escribe qué quiere cada pariente y cómo respondes con tacto.

answer.text: My mother asks whether that is all I'm having, so she is hinting that she wants me to eat more. My grandmother says that nobody ever asks for seconds these days, so she hopes that somebody will ask, and she would be pleased if we enjoyed her cooking. My uncle says that some relatives only call when they need something, so he is dropping a hint that I do not call him often enough. Mum, I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? Grandma, everything is delicious, so I'd happily take some leftovers home, if that's all right with you. Uncle, I'm sorry that I've been busy, but I'll call more often, won't I?
accepted: My mother asks whether that is all I'm having, so she is hinting that she wants me to eat more. My grandmother says that nobody ever asks for seconds these days, so she hopes that somebody will ask, and she would be pleased if we enjoyed her cooking. My uncle says that some relatives only call when they need something, so he is dropping a hint that I do not call him often enough. Mum, I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? Grandma, everything is delicious, so I'd happily take some leftovers home, if that's all right with you. Uncle, I'm sorry that I've been busy, but I'll call more often, won't I?

My mother asks if that is all I'm having, so she wants me to eat more. My grandmother complains that nobody asks for seconds these days, so she hopes that somebody will have another helping and enjoy her cooking. My uncle says that some relatives only call when they need something, so he is telling me that I don't call him often enough. Mum, I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? Grandma, I'm full, but I'd love to take some leftovers home, if you don't mind. Uncle, you're right, and I'm sorry, but I'll call you more often, won't I?

Mum's question means that she would like me to have more food. Grandma's comment about seconds shows that she hopes we will ask for more, because she cooked all afternoon. Uncle's remark means that I rarely call him, and he feels forgotten. Mum, I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? Grandma, everything is delicious, and I'll gladly have seconds of the dessert. Uncle, I'm sorry that I've been busy, but I'll call you this weekend, won't I? Thanks for the lovely dinner, everyone.

feedback.es: El texto interpreta las tres indirectas, responde con diplomacia a la madre y a la abuela, y cierra la respuesta al tío con una question tag.

origin.text: Cena familiar. Tres comentarios: a) tu madre dice «Is that all you're having?»; b) tu abuela dice «Nobody ever asks for seconds these days»; c) tu tío dice «Some relatives only call when they need something». Escribe en inglés (160–210 palabras): qué quiere decir cada uno y por qué, tu respuesta con tacto a tu madre y a tu abuela, y una respuesta al tío que termine con una question tag.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué insinúa el primo con su frase?

choices.text: That his brother only comes for the food, not the family.
That his brother should have brought something to the lunch.
That the whole family only meets when there is free food.

feedback.es: La mirada al hermano que llegó tarde convierte la generalización en un reproche concreto: solo aparece cuando hay comida gratis.

origin.text: At the end of a noisy family lunch, a cousin looks around the table at the empty dishes, then at his brother, who arrived after the main course, and says, 'Some people only visit when there is free food.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Hoy en día nadie repite plato, y hay muchas sobras.»

feedback.es: Ask for seconds es pedir repetir plato; la consecuencia lógica es que sobren muchos restos de comida.

origin.text: Nobody asks for ___ these days, so there are lots of leftovers in the fridge.

prompt.es: Elige la coletilla correcta: «El postre estuvo buenísimo, ¿verdad?»

choices.text: The dessert was lovely, isn't it?
The dessert was lovely, wasn't it?
The dessert was lovely, was it?

feedback.es: La coletilla repite el verbo de la frase en pasado (was → wasn't it) y, al ser de polaridad opuesta, pide coincidir.
